For amorphous SiO2, this activation energy was reported to be 0.38 eV
The TiO2-based memristor exhibits a switching voltage of around 1V and a switching field of 10^5 V/cm.
The NiO memristor exhibits a data retention time of 10^4 seconds at room temperature.
The NiO memristor can be fabricated with a feature size of less than 100 nm, enabling high integration density.

The MoS2 memristor exhibits forming-free switching with a high endurance of 10^7 cycles, low device-to-device variability (19.7% for set and 18.5% for reset), excellent retention time for 10 years and a remarkable wafer-scale crossbar arrays scalability
The NiO exhibits high endurance with more than 10^8 write/erase cycles without significant degradation.
The chalcogenide glass (GeSbTe) synaptic device can withstand over 10^6 write/erase cycles with negligible performance degradation.
The hafnium oxide (HfO2)-based memristor exhibits excellent retention characteristics, with a data retention time of over 10 years at room temperature.
